question: Which of the grammar's declared NAMED node types does the real corpus exercise, which does it never produce, and is each never-produced type reachable at all?

reachability.note: A named type the corpus never emits cannot be gated by that corpus. Each one below is probed with a minimal source, and the probe doubles as a fixture.

probes.why: grammar.js:97 `any_pragma_token: seq(identifier, $.pragma_value)` — a pragma whose name is not `solidity`.
grammar.js:645 — `do BLOCK while (expr);`. OpenZeppelin writes `while` loops, not `do`.
grammar.js:868 — a fixed-size array literal in a primary-expression position. OpenZeppelin never writes one.

grammar.js:193 — a member of `contract_declaration`'s `repeat(choice($._class_heritage, $.layout_specifier))`, so it belongs on the contract HEADER (Solidity 0.8.29 storage layout for errors). NOT on an error, which is where the first attempt put it.
grammar.js:103 — `pragma_value` is the `/[^;]+/` tail of any_pragma_token; `pragma abicoder v2;` is the commonest form.

grammar.js:682 — `state_location: choice('transient')`, reached only through `state_variable_declaration`'s `location` field. Solidity 0.8.28 transient storage; OpenZeppelin at this rev does not use it.
grammar.js — the `unicode` string prefix. OpenZeppelin's literals are all ASCII or `hex"…"` (10 of those).
grammar.js:416 — `yul_boolean: choice('true','false')`, a member of `_yul_literal`. OpenZeppelin's assembly is arithmetic, never boolean-valued.
grammar.js:395 — a `_yul_statement`. OpenZeppelin's 15 `yul_for_statement` loops all run to completion.
grammar.js:459 — `function id ( params ) -> results BLOCK`. OpenZeppelin inlines its assembly rather than defining Yul functions.
grammar.js:396 — `yul_label: seq($.identifier, ":")`, a `_yul_statement`. A labelled block is the only construct that makes one.
grammar.js:394 — `yul_leave: 'leave'`, a bare `_yul_statement`. OpenZeppelin's 5 `yul_switch_statement`s always take a case branch.

negativeControls.why: `constant_variable_declaration` is a `_declaration` member, i.e. FILE scope (grammar.js:155-166); inside a contract the same text is a `state_variable_declaration`. The positive probe only worked once this was read off the rule's parent.
`pragma_value` is the tail of `any_pragma_token` only; the `solidity` form produces `solidity_version`.
a Solidity `true` is a `boolean_literal > true`, not a `yul_boolean`.

the MODERN spelling `S({a: 1})` is a `call_expression` with `call_struct_argument` children; only the pre-0.8.8 `S { a: 1 }` is a `struct_expression`. Both spellings exist in the corpus (13 and 33) and they are different node types.
`layout_specifier` belongs to a contract header, not to any declaration.
grammar.js:171 — `type name is primitive_type;`. Without `is` the source does not parse at all, so this negative also confirms the type is not produced by a broken parse.
Yul syntax outside an `assembly_statement` is a parse error, not a silently-accepted Yul node.

reachability.negativeControlNote: The probes are only worth reading if they can fail. Each is paired with a negative control that must NOT produce the type; a control that reports the type present means the probe reports presence for the wrong reason.

yulIsNotUnderRepresented.claim: the corpus under-represents Solidity inline assembly
yulIsNotUnderRepresented.verdict: REFUTED — the opposite is true, and the lane is built accordingly
yulIsNotUnderRepresented.consequence: Yul is analysed as a first-class sub-language: its own functions, variables, calls, paths and loops each get a case. Ruling Yul out would have removed more edges than the entire contract layer's call graph.

howToRead: damaged/errorNodes/missingNodes are the PARSER's, not the analyzer's: a MISSING node is a token the parser INSERTED to keep going, so it is a fabrication with no error attached and is the class worth reading first.

declaredNamed is read from the vendored src/node-types.json (124 named). runtime.nodeTypeCount is 531 because the wasm's own type array also holds supertypes and inlined tokens; the two numbers are different questions and are not comparable.

neverExercisedList is a property of THIS DRAW, not of the language. The same instrument at --sample 60 reported 27; at the full production count it is the list above. Never quote the draw's number as the corpus's.
